entry.content:
Dear colleagues,

We are pleased to announce that the 6th International Bicycle & Motorcycle Dynamics Conference (BMD 2027) will take place from 9 to 11 June 2027 in Lyon, France.

BMD brings together the international community of scientists, researchers and engineers working in the broad field of bicycle and motorcycle dynamics and control. The conference will feature a single-track scientific programme, poster sessions, and dedicated opportunities for discussion and networking.

Further information, including the Call for Papers, conference website and registration details, will be announced in the coming months.

We look forward to welcoming you to Lyon!

Best regards,

The BMD 2027 Organising Committee

entry.content: Unfortunately, the 2026 conference will not occur in Japan this year due to unforeseen circumstances. The scientific committee is now seeking a host for the next conference symposium. To try keep close to the three-year cycle, we hope to arrange the next conference as soon as feasible. If you are interested in being the next host or know someone who might be, please contact Jason K. Moore at j.k.moore@tudelft.nl.

entry.content:
Today marks the 1 year anniversary of the BMD 2023 conference in Delft and we are very pleased to announce that the proceedings book is now officially published. The proceedings is a 464 page volume containing 60 extended abstracts from all the presentations and 28 peer reviewed full papers.

BMD 2023 Proceedings Cover

You may download your copy here:

https://books.open.tudelft.nl/home/catalog/book/121

We would like to extend our sincere thanks to all of the contributions that made this possible: the researchers, authors, and reviewers and especially to the support of TU Delft OPEN Publishing.

This is the first time we have published a complete proceedings of the conference and we hope that you all find the result as valuable as we do. You can also browse each individual article along with the peer reviews on the Orvium community page.

We hope to see you all in Hamamatsu in 2026!

Sincerely,

Jason K. Moore, Edwin de Vries, Andrew Dressel, and Leila Alizadehsaravi
